## Why

ork's spec check (S116) keeps its verdicts in daemon memory, because ork may not keep tracking state of its own (ork non-goal C06). The owner decided on 2026-10-26 to keep that cache for now and asked for both: a durable readiness record in slicer as well. u4 already defines "well specified" (files, failing tests, steps, checks, no open owner decision), and `slicer next` skips items with an empty Implement or Check, but nothing records that a spec check passed, or invalidates that when the spec changes.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ops.py`, `src/slicer/cli.py`: a readiness command or field.
- `src/slicer/model.py`: the stored verdict and its spec digest.
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/agents.md`.

## Implement

Proposed, for the owner: `slicer ready ID --by NAME [--note TEXT]` records a verdict with a digest of the slice's sections. `show --json` and `list --json` report `ready: true|false|stale`; any section edit makes it `stale`. `next --ready` may prefer ready items. Owner decisions needed: the command name, and whether `next` filters or only sorts.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-26: the command is `slicer ready ID --by NAME [--note TEXT]`. `next --ready` sorts items whose readiness is `true` first and does not filter on readiness.
